summary: Ajahn Sucitto works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Warwick (~1968–1971) and under Ajahn Sumedho in 1977, later serving as abbot of Cittaviveka from 1992 to 2014.

Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Ajahn Sumedho studied at the University of Washington, UC Berkeley (~1961–1963), and under Ajahn Chah (1967–1977). He founded Cittaviveka, and served as abbot at Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and Amaravati (1984–2010).

Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a pupil under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and held a post as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.
Akhil Rajeev P is active in computational Indology. He has held posts at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, Akifumi Naito studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji-ha Shōgakuin, and under Gadjin M. Nagao (1979–2002). He held posts at Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies, Ryukoku University (attested 2003–2009), Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist College.

Akihiko Akamatsu works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Yuichi Kajiyama (~1975–1983), at Kyoto University (1976), and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University/University of Paris (~1979–1983). He held faculty and administrative leadership posts at Kyoto University (1983–2023).
Akihiro Oda works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, where he also held posts as a lecturer (attested 1992) and as Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Akiko Kikuchi works in Buddhist studies. She studied as a research student at Minobusan University (attested 2026) and served as a professor at Musashino University (attested 2026).

Akimichi Eda specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang.
Akio Donohashi works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1974) and served as a professor at Kobe University (1990–1991).

Akio Minoura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Otani University as associate professor (attested 2007–2013) and faculty (attested 2026), and conducted overseas research at Stanford University (2012–2013).

Akio Tanabe works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2006). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (professor, 2015).

Akira Fujieda specialized in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), where he later served as professor (1968), and held visiting professorships at the University of Copenhagen (1970) and UC Berkeley (1988).
Akira Hataya works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 2014).

Akira Hirakawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Shoson Miyamoto and at the University of Tokyo, where he was professor (1962–1975). He also taught at Waseda University (1975–1985) and led the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.

Akira Miyaji specializes in Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Nagoya University (~1964–1991) and held posts at Hirosaki University (~1974–1978), Nagoya University (~1978–2007), Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art (~2007–2013), and Ryukoku University (2013).

Akira Mukai works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Hokkaido University, where he served as an assistant (attested 1978), and later became a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto and Heidelberg universities, holding posts at Kyoto University (1959), Osaka University of Foreign Studies (1966–1973), Osaka University (1980–1992), and Ryukoku University (1992).

Akira Sadakata works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, the University of Paris, and under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura. He served at Tokai University as associate professor (~1971–1979) and professor (~1979–2007).

Akira Saitō specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and ANU under Jikido Takasaki. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (2000–2016) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2016–2021).
